answers.explanation: 99% of requests are faster than the p99. The remaining 1% are at least that slow.
A few very slow requests can hide in an average. Percentiles tell you how many users saw which delay.
Half of requests are faster than the p50: it's the typical experience.
The page is as slow as its slowest call. With 10 calls, the chance at least one is slow is about 1 - 0.99^10, roughly 10%. This is tail latency amplification.
The users with the most data or activity hit the tail most often, so the tail is where your best customers live.
Both are usually written on percentiles, like "p99 below 200 ms, 99.9% of the time."
Waiting time doesn't grow gently. Around 70% busy queues form in bursts, and near 100% they run away.
You'll meet head-of-line blocking again in TCP, where one lost segment stalls every byte behind it.
